home.q: Do you work with primary and secondary schools?
home.a: Yes. Lessons can be adapted to different age groups, so students build practical digital skills at an appropriate pace.
Students explore product design (UI/UX), web development with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, and how to prompt AI tools responsibly to help plan and build.

home.q: What does Assessly help our school manage?
home.a: Student and class records, question banks, tests, exams and results are brought into a shared assessment workflow.

home.q: How can our school become a partner?
home.a: Enquire with your school name, your role and a short outline of your current process. We can discuss a suitable next step.

products.q: Can we discuss our school’s assessment needs first?
products.a: Yes. Use the enquiry form to describe your school and the assessment tasks you want to organise. Avoid sharing student records in your message.

partner.q: Do we need an existing coding programme?
partner.a: No existing programme is needed to begin a conversation. Tell us what your school already offers and what your students are ready to explore.

partner.q: Can a pathway suit different age groups?
partner.a: Yes. Project scope, pace and activities can be discussed around primary or secondary learners and their current experience.

partner.q: Can we ask about Assessly as well?
partner.a: Yes. Mention Assessly in your enquiry if you also want to discuss students, classes, question banks, exams and results.

contact.q: I want to discuss a school partnership. Which form should I use?
contact.a: You can choose School partnership above, or use the dedicated school enquiry form on Become a Partner for more detail about learners and pathways.

contact.q: Can I ask about Assessly here?
contact.a: Yes. Choose Assessly as your enquiry type and describe your question about students, classes, question banks, tests, exams or results.
